Nudge preset settings toward the published patterns

Source: R/sim-tools.R
wgh_tune_preset.Rd

A light, guided calibration. It simulates a modest cohort, compares a few patterns with wgh_targets and adjusts the settings that drive each pattern most directly: the BMI-for-age mean and spread (overweight and obesity), the under-5 adiposity shift, and attendance by age group. It repeats this a few times. It is meant for the package maintainer and for Book 2 Chapter 3 readers who want to build their own preset, not for formal estimation.

Usage

wgh_tune_preset(
  preset = "wgh_like",
  n_children = 15000,
  iterations = 3,
  seed = 99
)

Arguments

preset

Starting preset name or settings list.

n_children

Size of each trial cohort.

iterations

Number of adjustment rounds.

seed

Seed for the trial cohorts.

Value

The adjusted settings list, with an attribute "history".

Examples

# \donttest{
s <- wgh_tune_preset("wgh_like", n_children = 6000, iterations = 2)
s$baz_mean
#>      Male    Female 
#> 0.9516337 0.2850429 
# }
